# Our Data

## Primary Dataset: Austin Crime Reports 2003-Present
## Secondary Dataset: Key Economic Indicators in Austin 2007-2025
### Source: data.gov

```{r, message=FALSE, echo = FALSE}

# Load in data
crimes <- read.csv("austin.csv")
econ <- read.csv("austin_econ.csv")

```

# Key Objective
Explain key objective

## Key Variables
* __Highest Offense Description__: Tells us what the crime is. Important for us to be able to judge severity and type of crime.
* __Location Type__: Tells us what type of place the crime occurred. Important to make distinctions between places like homes, stores, etc.
* __District__: Gives general area of the crime in Austin. Allows us to understand where crimes are occurring in the city.
* __Occurred Time__: Tells us when the crime occurred so we can determine if crime is more common during certain times of day.
* __Report Time__: Tells us when the crime was reported and can be combined with occurred time to understand how it takes certain areas to report crimes.

## Pre-Processing
* Grouping times, so instead of looking at specific times we can analyze times of day.
* Converting datetime character vectors to datetime object to make datetime data columns more usable.
* Create a new column, Net.Response.Date.Time, which measures the time between the date and time between when the crime occurred and when it was reported.
* 

# Visualizations

## Scatterplot

```{r, , message=FALSE}
plot(econ$Retail.Gasoline.Price.TX, econ$Retail.Diesel.Price.TX,
     main= "Gas vs Diesel Prices in Texas",
     xlab = "Gas Price", ylab = "Diesel Price",
     pch = 19, cex = .7, col = "blue",
     mgp = c(2, .7, 0),
     xlim = c(1.5, 5.5), ylim = c(1.5, 5.5))

```

## Interpretation
As gas prices have increased, diesel prices have generally gone with them. There is a moderately strong correlation between diesel and gas prices, allowing us to better understand Texas' economy. By showing this strong correlation, we are better prepared to look at how vehicle crimes have changed over time.

## Boxplot -- Average Time to Report Crime in Austin (2003-2025)

```{r, , message=FALSE}
#PreProcessing
library(hms)
crimes$Occurred.Date.Time <- as.POSIXct(crimes$Occurred.Date.Time, format = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M")
crimes$Report.Date.Time <- as.POSIXct(crimes$Report.Date.Time, format = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M")
crimes$NetResponse.Date.Time <- crimes$Report.Date.Time - crimes$Occurred.Date.Time

#Plot
bp <- boxplot(crimes$NetResponse.Date.Time[crimes$NetResponse.Date.Time > 0], outline = FALSE,
        yaxt = "n", 
        ylab = "Report Time (HRS:MIN:SEC)", 
        main = "Average Time to Report Crime in Austin, TX (2003-2025)",
        sub = "Zero Duration Excluded | Outliers Removed From Plot"
        )

axis(2, at = axTicks(2), labels = as.hms(time_breaks))

# Add labels for median, Q1, and Q3
stats <- bp$stats
rownames(stats) <- c("Lower Whisker", "Q1 (25%)", "Median", "Q3 (75%)", "Upper Whisker")

text(x = 0.7, y = stats[2,1], labels = paste("Q1:", as.hms(stats[2,1], 1)), pos = 3, col = "red")
text(x = 0.7, y = stats[3,1], labels = paste("Median:", as.hms(stats[3,1], 1)), pos = 3, col = "blue")
text(x = 0.7, y = stats[4,1], labels = paste("Q3:", as.hms(stats[4,1], 1)), pos = 3, col = "darkgreen")
#line and % at 48 hours
percentile_48 <- round(ecdf(crimes$NetResponse.Date.Time[crimes$NetResponse.Date.Time > 0])(60*60*48)*100, 1)
abline(h = 48 * 60 * 60, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
text(x = 1.25, y = 48 * 60 * 60, labels = paste0("48 Hours: ", percentile_48, "th Percentile"), 
     pos = 3, col = "red", offset = 1)

```

## Interpretation
The vast majority (74%) of crimes are reported within 48 hours of reportedly being committed. The median time to report a crime is about 11 and a half hours. Additionally, the time needed to report a crime is heavily right-skewed, indicating significant room for study on what crimes are not reported quickly, and why. 


## Heatmap -- Crime by Month and District

```{r, , message=FALSE}
#Pulling Months and labelling as text
heatmap_crimes <- crimes[,c("Occurred.Date", "APD.District")]
heatmap_crimes$month <- substr(as.character(heatmap_crimes$Occurred.Date), 0, 2)
heatmap_crimes$month <- factor(heatmap_crimes$month, labels = c("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"), levels = c("01", "02", "03", "04", "05", "06", "07", "08", "09", "10", "11", "12"))
heatmap_crimes$month <- factor(heatmap_crimes$month, levels = rev(levels(heatmap_crimes$month)))
heatmap_crimes <- heatmap_crimes[heatmap_crimes$APD.District != "",]

#Turn data into table object
count_table <- table(heatmap_crimes$month, heatmap_crimes$APD.District)
count_table <- count_table[rowSums(count_table) >= 1500, 
               colSums(count_table) >= 1500]
count_table

par(mar = c(7, 6, 8, 6))  # Increased margins: c(bottom, left, top, right)
#Plot the table as a heatmap
heatmap(as.matrix(count_table), 
        Colv = NA, 
        Rowv = NA,
        col = colorRampPalette(c("pink", "red"))(50),
        ylab = "Month",
        xlab = "District | Min. 1500 Reported Crimes",
        main = "Crime by Month and District | Austin, TX (2003-2025)")
```

## Interpretation
In general, the displayed districts are the only districts in Austin with any significant crime. All districts not displayed have at most an average of 5.68 crimes per month reported. While this seems moderately high, the dataset includes crimes like petty theft, false alarms, and civil disturbance which are ultimately not that serious compared to widespread crime. Thus, it is reasonable to say that the highest concentration of crime in Austin is in districts 1-8, 88, D, and S. We can use this information to further explore the interactions crime has with the general economy in these areas.
